newsitem.title: SPAIN: CanalSatelite unveils Spain's digital platform.
newsitem.headline: CanalSatelite unveils Spain's digital platform.

text.p: Spain's CanalSatellite Digital unveiled its digital television platform on Thursday and will begin to sell it on Friday, despite a planned revamping of the law that could hinder the nation's first such project.

Jesus de Polanco, president of Promotora de Informaciones, S.A. (Prisa) and of CanalSatellite, said the companies that participate in CanalSatellite had invested 65 billion pesetas in the project and it would be the government's fault if it failed.
CanalSatellite comprises Prisa and Canal Plus via the Sogecable holding, as well as TV station Antena 3.
The government has announced there should only be one type of decoder for all the new pay-TV channels, allowing viewers to tune into not just one but all platforms available with the same equipment.
"We won't tolerate, even if it costs us a fortune, that there is an abuse of power," said Polanco of the government's new stance.

"The specifications set out by the government haven't been invented yet," he said, adding that CanalSatellite's decoders are approved by the European Union and can receive 950 channels from up to 15 different platforms.
Polanco said he was confident the government would eventually back down on its technical demands.

He added he was open to negotiate with the operators of the second planned digital platform on the use of a common decoder. This group is comprised of Telefonica, Radio and Television of Spain (RTVE), Mexican group Televisa and several regional television channels.
CanalSatellite's project has the lucrative football TV rights via Antena 3, as well as Canal Plus's established pay-TV.
The new satellite platform will offer 25 TV channels and services from tomorrow, and hopes to obtain 150,000-200,000 subscribers during the first year.
